sections.html:
The Bellefonte office records the deeds, mortgages and related papers for every parcel in Centre County, and it acts as the county's agent for realty transfer tax. Its job is to record, protect, preserve and reproduce the legal documents tied to real estate here.

Official land records begin in 1800, the year the county was formed. The office also records notary commissions, oaths and military discharge papers, and it collects fees for the Affordable Housing Fund and the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts.

The Recorder of Deeds is in the Willowbank Office Building, 414 Holmes Street, Suite 1, Bellefonte, PA 16823. Call 814-355-6801. Doors are open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

  • Documents are taken as close to 5 p.m. as practical, and there are no Saturday or evening hours.
  • You can mail papers in, as long as every recording requirement is met and the right fee is enclosed.
  • A deed that still needs its UPI can go straight to the Assessment Office, which stamps it and forwards it to the recorder.
  • E-recording runs through Simplifile and CSC.

Return time is usually one to two days, though holidays, volume and staffing can stretch it. If nothing has come back after three weeks, contact whoever recorded the paper.

A deed or mortgage costs $71.25 for four pages and four names, plus $2 for each added page and $0.50 for each added name. The Commonwealth sets these fees through the General Assembly, and they can change.

Pay recording fees with cash, check or card. Cards add $3.99 or 2.95% of the transaction, whichever is higher.

The rate is 1% to the state and 1% local on the consideration or value, with three exceptions: State College Borough at 3%, Ferguson Township at 2.75% and Taylor Township at 1.5%. The state share goes to the Department of Revenue, and the local share splits between the municipality and the school district.

The office refuses a deed unless the tax due comes with it. Buyer and seller usually share the bill under the sales agreement. Still, if the amount paid is challenged later, the new owner is the one on the hook for any gap. You don't need separate checks for the state and local shares. Make every check payable to the Centre County Recorder of Deeds.

For a house near the University Park campus, the municipality changes the tax on the same price, so confirm whether the property is in the borough or a township before you set a net figure.

sections.h2: Exempt transfers and the Statement of Value
sections.html:
Exempt transfers include those between spouses, from parent to child, from grandparent to grandchild, and among brothers and sisters. A transfer between ex-spouses also qualifies. Most nonprofit corporations get no exemption. Anything out of the ordinary is a question for an attorney.

The Statement of Value is a state form giving the property's value or the reason no tax is due. Staff pass every one along to the Department of Revenue. You need one whenever the true value isn't on the deed, such as a $1 consideration, or when tax isn't paid at recording. An exemption claim not based on family relationship must give its reason, and a deed on land in more than one municipality must show the local tax split in dollars.

sections.h2: Getting a copy of a deed
sections.html:
Anyone can look at a deed or mortgage, because only military discharges are kept private. Ordering a copy costs $0.50 per page, and certifying it adds $1.50. Send the owner's full name, the property location, a rough purchase date and a self-addressed stamped envelope. If the original is lost, a certified copy takes its place.

The county also runs a subscription portal, WEBIA, covering the recorder, register of wills, tax claim and maps. Records from before 1989 sit in separate Deed, Mortgage and Miscellaneous books, and everything since 1989 is in Record Books, which helps when a title searcher asks for a book and page.

Staff won't search records for you or write a deed. After a death, a surviving spouse who held title as tenants by the entireties generally needn't record anything right away. The next deed or mortgage explains the death. Other forms of ownership can call for different steps, so see an attorney.

The county gives filers ten instructions, and most failures trace back to names, notary blocks or the UPI.

  • Names in the caption, signature block and acknowledgment must match exactly. Variants like John J. Doe and J Joseph Doe cause rejections.
  • The acknowledgment must show county, state, date, the person or officer appearing, and the notary's signature, seal and expiration date. It shouldn't predate the document date.
  • The written amount must match the numeric amount on deeds and mortgages.
  • Every deed needs a pre-authorized UPI from the Centre County Assessment Office before recording. Call 814-355-6721 with questions.
  • List the property's municipality, and every one if there are several.
  • Leave a one-inch by three-inch space for the recorder's stamp at the top of page one.
  • Include a self-addressed, postage-paid envelope big enough for the return.

Centre County is home to the State College metropolitan area, with Bellefonte as the seat and State College as the largest borough. About 157,393 people lived here in 2025, spread over roughly 1,109 square miles. Owner-occupied homes had a median value of $323,500 for 2020 to 2024, and just 61.8% of homes are owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $1,207. A seller in one township may face a different school district tax than a neighbor a few miles away. The county's Common Level Ratio was 6.10 as of July 1, 2026.

Get the UPI early from the Assessment Office. It is a $10.00 stamp paid by separate check. Compare every name with the prior deed and look over the notary block. Settle how the transfer tax gets paid, then bring a single check to the Recorder of Deeds. If you can't be there at closing, e-record through Simplifile or CSC or mail the package with a return envelope. Recording protects the buyer, and it keeps tax bills from going to the old owner.

faqs.q: Do Centre County buyers and sellers need separate transfer tax checks?
faqs.a: No. Separate checks for state and local transfer tax aren't necessary. All checks are payable to the Centre County Recorder of Deeds, and the office accepts cash or check for fees.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax in State College?
faqs.a: State College Borough is 3% of the consideration or value, compared with 1% state plus 1% local in most of the county. Ferguson Township is 2.75% and Taylor Township is 1.5%.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed without a UPI in Centre County?
faqs.a: No. Every deed needs a UPI issued by the Centre County Assessment Office, sold as a $10.00 stamp, before it can be recorded. A separate check payable to the County of Centre covers it.

faqs.q: Can the Recorder of Deeds change a deed that is already recorded?
faqs.a: No. Once recorded, a document can't be altered. A new deed showing the change has to be recorded, and a wrong name or description is usually fixed with a deed of correction prepared by an attorney.

faqs.q: Do I have to record a deed at all in Centre County?
faqs.a: A signed and delivered deed is valid, but recording protects the buyer. If it is left off the record, the former owner could still borrow against the property, and tax bills may keep going to the old owner.
